create.name: Great Tree Zen Women's Temple
create.bio:
Great Tree Zen Women's Temple, also known as Daijuji, is a Soto Zen temple in the hills outside Asheville, North Carolina, with an address in the small community of Alexander. Its founder and abbess, Rev. Teijo Munnich, studied with Dainin Katagiri from 1975 until his death in 1990, was ordained as a priest in 1981 and trained at Hokyoji in Minnesota, Tassajara and Hosshinji in Japan. She first imagined a residential practice place for women in 1983; the temple was incorporated as a church in the early 2000s and opened at its present site in 2005. Rev. Chimyo Atkinson, ordained by Teijo and given Dharma transmission in 2015 after training periods in Japan and Iowa, also teaches there.

Residential training is for women, while everything else is open to people of every gender. The weekly round includes early-morning zazen on Zoom, a short tonglen practice, Thursday evening sitting and Saturday morning zazen with a talk, in the hall or online. Monthly full-moon gatherings, an introduction to Zen on Zoom and a family meditation morning sit alongside sesshin of two to five days, spring and autumn practice periods and residencies. Events are offered by donation, and the temple shares its chant book and many recorded talks freely.

courses.title: Weekly Zazen, Tonglen and Saturday Lectures
courses.description: The temple's regular week: early zazen on Zoom on Wednesdays, a half-hour tonglen practice on Thursday mornings, Thursday evening sitting and Saturday morning zazen followed by a talk, in the hall or online. Monthly full-moon ceremonies and a Zoom introduction to Zen are also held.

courses.title: Sesshin at Great Tree
courses.description: Retreats of two to five days with zazen, work practice, formal oryoki meals and optional private interviews with the teacher, joined at the temple or on Zoom. Upcoming dates include a Rohatsu sesshin in early December.

courses.title: Practice Periods
courses.description: A four-week winter practice period and longer spring and autumn periods, in person or on Zoom, built around a weekly early-morning sitting and study group and a personal commitment to regular practice.

courses.title: Women's Residency
courses.description: Residential training for women who want to live at the temple and follow its schedule of meditation, study and work. Applicants attend a five-day sesshin first, then apply and interview.

courses.title: Family Practice
courses.description: A monthly Sunday family meditation with a short sitting, a teaching and activities such as storytelling, movement and crafts, plus an annual family retreat and festive gatherings. All ages are welcome.

free_resources.title: Great Tree Chant Book
free_resources.description: The temple's book of Soto Zen chants and scriptures used in its services, free to download as a PDF.
